steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building React components with state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. These are essential for building React components with state management.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the main Tabs component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Tabs that returns null for now. This will be the main container component for our tabs.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure to export the component.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and useState from 'react'

// Create the Tabs component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should see a Tabs component defined that returns null and is exported.
successCriteria: A Tabs component is defined and exported, returning null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main Tabs component that will serve as the container for our tab system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named Tabs that returns null and is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tabs component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a component named Tabs that returns null and is exported.

steps.title: Create the TabList component
steps.instruction: Create a function component named TabList that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a new component function called TabList. Inside, return null.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a TabList component that returns null.
successCriteria: A TabList component is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the TabList component. It will later hold the tab buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you define a component named TabList that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match. Create a component named TabList that returns null.

steps.title: Create the Tab component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Tab that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called Tab that returns null. This will be the individual tab button component.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Tab component function is created that returns null.
successCriteria: The Tab component is defined as a function that returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the Tab component. This will serve as the building block for individual tab buttons.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a function named Tab that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tab component wasn't created correctly. Create a function named Tab that returns null.

steps.title: Create the TabPanels component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TabPanels that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called TabPanels that returns null. This will be a placeholder component to hold the content panels.
steps.expectedOutcome: A TabPanels component is created that returns null, serving as a placeholder for future content panels.
successCriteria: A functional component named TabPanels is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the TabPanels component. This will serve as the container for the content panels in our tabs system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named TabPanels that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanels component wasn't created correctly. Please create a functional component named TabPanels that returns null.

steps.title: Create the TabPanel component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TabPanel that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called TabPanel that returns null.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a TabPanel component that returns null.
successCriteria: A TabPanel component is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the TabPanel component. This will serve as the container for individual tab content panels.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named TabPanel that returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to create a component called TabPanel that returns null.

steps.title: Add activeTab state to Tabs component
steps.instruction: Inside the Tabs component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'activeTab' initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState(0) and destructure the returned array to get the state variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component will have an activeTab state variable that tracks which tab is currently selected, starting with the first tab (index 0).
successCriteria: The Tabs component contains a useState call that declares 'activeTab' state initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the activeTab state to track the currently selected tab.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an initial value of 0 and naming the state variable 'activeTab'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tabs component doesn't have the activeTab state yet. Remember to use useState(0) inside the Tabs component.

steps.title: Add structure to Tabs component with children
steps.instruction: Update the Tabs component to accept a children prop and render it inside a div wrapper.
steps.hint: Add a children parameter to your Tabs component function and return a div containing {children}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tabs component will accept children and render them inside a div element.
successCriteria: Tabs component returns a div containing {children}
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The Tabs component now accepts and renders children, which is essential for compound components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your Tabs component accepts children as a prop and returns a div containing {children}.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. The Tabs component needs to accept children and render them inside a div.

steps.title: Add structure to TabList component
steps.instruction: Update the TabList component to accept a children prop and render it inside a div element with role='tablist'.
steps.hint: The TabList component should receive children as a prop and wrap them in a div with role='tablist'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TabList component will accept children and render them inside a div with role='tablist'.
successCriteria: TabList component accepts children prop and returns a div with role='tablist' containing the children.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The TabList component now properly accepts and renders children with the correct role.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the TabList component accepts children as a prop and renders them inside a div with role='tablist'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabList component should accept children as a prop and render them inside a div with role='tablist'. Check your implementation.

steps.title: Add structure and click handler to Tab component
steps.instruction: Update the Tab component to accept index and onClick props, and render a button with an onClick handler that calls the onClick prop with the index.
steps.hint: The Tab component should receive props and return a button element. The button's onClick handler should call the onClick prop with the index value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Tab component will be ready to render interactive tab buttons that can trigger tab changes.
successCriteria: Tab component accepts index and onClick props, returns a button with onClick handler that calls onClick(index).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The Tab component now accepts props and handles clicks properly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the Tab component accepts both index and onClick props, and the button's onClick handler calls onClick with the index.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Tab component needs to accept index and onClick props and render a button with an onClick handler that calls onClick(index).

steps.title: Add structure to TabPanels component
steps.instruction: Update the TabPanels component to accept a children prop and render it inside a div element.
steps.hint: The TabPanels component should receive children as a prop and return a div containing those children.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TabPanels component will be able to wrap and display child components passed to it.
successCriteria: TabPanels component accepts children prop and returns a div containing children
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The TabPanels component now properly accepts and renders children.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure TabPanels accepts children as a prop and returns a div containing those children.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanels component needs to accept children as a prop and render them inside a div.

steps.title: Add structure to TabPanel component
steps.instruction: Create the TabPanel component as a function that accepts index and activeTab props, and conditionally renders children when index matches activeTab.
steps.hint: The TabPanel should return its children only when the index prop equals the activeTab prop. Otherwise, return null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TabPanel component will render its content only when its index matches the active tab.
successCriteria: TabPanel component is defined with index and activeTab props, and conditionally renders children based on index matching activeTab.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The TabPanel component now conditionally renders content based on the active tab.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the TabPanel component, but check that it correctly uses the index and activeTab props to conditionally render children.
steps.feedbackWrong: The TabPanel component is missing or doesn't properly handle conditional rendering based on index and activeTab.
